page.description: LibreELEC editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: A minimal Linux appliance built on Buildroot and BusyBox that runs one application — Kodi — on a read-only system with a writable overlay. Ships with Kodi 21.3 and Linux kernel 6.16.x.
pros: Just enough OS: read-only system, no package manager or bloat.
Auto-update tracks minor versions (12.2.x) without user intervention.
Two x86_64 images: modern Mesa/GBM and legacy Xorg.
Per-artifact SHA-256 metadata endpoint (?mirrorlist) needs no download.
cons: x86_64 only — no i386 support since OpenELEC 5.x.
Dual boot unsupported: installer requires a dedicated disk.
NVIDIA hardware discouraged; 340.xx driver dropped from legacy in 12.2.
No published signature — matching SHA-256 does not prove authenticity.
page.previewNote: No screenshot with a reusable licence was confirmed for LibreELEC; the page shows the logo only. No image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted.
page.status: Write the .img.gz to a USB stick with dd or the LibreELEC USB-SD Creator; writing erases the stick. Boot the target machine from that media and install to a dedicated internal disk. The .tar file is update-only — it cannot be written to a stick.

editions.name: Generic
editions.description: The modern Mesa/GBM image for current PCs — labelled 'Generic PC (no NVIDIA support)' on the download page.
editions.usbNote: 275 MB compressed image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Legacy
editions.description: The older Xorg image for older PCs and NVIDIA GPUs; the NVIDIA 340.xx driver was dropped from this variant in 12.2.
editions.usbNote: 482 MB compressed image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.
